 Commercial LPG cylinder price hiked by ₹10 to ₹2,820 from November 1
 LPG price landscape in 2026 has witnessed unprecedented volatility.
 By ANI 
 Updated - November 01, 2026 at 09:57 AM. 
 | 
 New Delhi
 × Share
 WhatsApp X Facebook LinkedIn Messenger Reddit Mail https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/commercial-lpg-cylinder-price-hiked-by-10-to-2820-from-november-1/article71652108.ece Copy 
 Siliguri: A delivery worker arranges domestic LPG cylinders on a commercial vehicle for distribution to households
 | Photo Credit:
 -
 The price of a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder has been increased by ₹10 to ₹2,820 from Sunday. The 19-kg commercial cylinder was priced at ₹2,810 on October 1. With the latest revision, the price has increased by ₹10 over the past month.
 This marks the third consecutive monthly increase in commercial gas rates, dealing a blow to the hospitality sector, eateries, and commercial vendors right in the middle of the peak festive season. Meanwhile, the price of a 5-kg Free Trade LPG (FTL) cylinder for a new connection stands at Rs 1,903, while a 5-kg FTL refill is priced at ₹782, according to the revised rate list.
 The LPG price landscape in 2026 has witnessed unprecedented volatility, driven largely by external geopolitical shocks. Prices saw a massive single-month surge of nearly ₹1,000 per cylinder on May 1, pushing commercial LPG rates above the ₹3,000 mark to around ₹3,071.50 in Delhi.
 Relief followed in July and August, when oil marketing companies announced cumulative cuts totalling ₹380 per cylinder, bringing substantial respite to commercial consumers during mid-summer. The trend reversed again during the festive season with consecutive hikes. After marginal upward adjustments on September 1 and a ₹65 per cylinder hike on October 1, prices were raised again on November 1 by ₹10 to ₹17 across metros, taking the Delhi rate to ₹2,820.
 Also read
 LPG under recovery may rise to ₹370/cylinder in December 2026
 The elevated gas and fuel import costs throughout 2026 are largely driven by escalating tensions and naval disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz,  the critical maritime choke point through which a significant portion of Middle Eastern crude and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) passes.
 India depends on imports for roughly half of its natural gas and LPG consumption, with a major share of LPG shipments originating from Gulf producers that transit through the Strait. Operational bottlenecks and heightened security risks in the Strait earlier this year triggered a contraction in global LPG supply, leading to freight spikes. The higher shipping risk premiums, combined with global crude volatility — with Brent hovering above $110 per barrel — and elevated international Saudi Aramco contract prices, have kept domestic commercial fuel rates elevated despite minor month-on-month adjustments.
